content:
Jess: Quick design review request — invite modal tweaks for RBAC and audit navigation. TL;DR: 1) prefill role suggestions based on org context, 2) inline explanation for 'persistent access', 3) move SSO toggle off the main row into a compact pill, 4) small audit-log jump link from invite detail.

Eli: Nice. Can you drop a screenshot or a quick mock?

Jess: Pasted a mini-ASCII mock below (super rough):

Jess: ```
Invite to Redwood Cloud
[Email input] [Role dropdown ▾] [Suggest: Viewer, Analyst] [Persist Access: (i) ] [SSO: • ] [Send invite]

Role dropdown expanded:
- Viewer — read-only
- Analyst — read + query
- Admin — full access
```

Tara: Love prefill. Question: what exactly does "Persist Access" mean? We need a one-line help text, not full modal copy.

Jess: Agreed. Proposal: helper text beneath the toggle: "Persistent access keeps the role until revoked — ideal for service accounts or long-term contractors." Keep it short.

Sam: Accessibility nits:
- Toggle needs aria-label and keyboard focus order.
- Role suggestions should be announced when dropdown opens.
- The small 'i' explainer should be reachable via keyboard and screen reader.

Eli: For placement: moving SSO into a pill keeps row compact, but might hide it from admins skimming the modal. Maybe show SSO pill collapsed with a tooltip showing account provisioning state.

Jess: Good call. Behavior idea: if org SSO enforced, pill shows "SSO enforced" in red and blocks persistent access toggle. If optional, pill is gray and opens to more options.

Tara: Copy tweak suggestion: change "Persistent access" -> "Keep access until revoked" (verb-first tends to be clearer). Thoughts?

Sam: +1 on verb-first. Shorter and clearer for screen reader users. Also suggest visible focus ring on the SSO pill.

Eli: On audit log jump: add a tiny link under the invite summary: "View invite events" that opens audit-log filtered to the invitee's email and the invite action. Saves a search.

Jess: Implementation note for engineers: audit link should encode filters as query params, e.g. 
```
/audit?user_email=jane%40example.com&action=invite
```
That keeps the console stateless and easy to share.

Sam: Accessibility for that link: label should be "View invite events for [email]" so screen readers get context. Also ensure the link target has an H1 that reflects the filter.

Tara: Role matrix spacing debate: do we show compact 4-up rows by default or expanded single column? I'd prefer default compact but add a "dense/comfortable" toggle in settings. Admins can pick.

Eli: Agree on a density toggle in org settings. But in the invite modal, default to comfortable spacing if the user has never toggled density (to avoid surprises).

Jess: UX constraints: keep modal height <= 640px to avoid scrolling on smaller screens. That will limit how many inline explainer lines we can show. Use ellipses and a hover card for more details.

Sam: Keyboard nav specifics I want documented for devs:
1) Tab to email field -> Enter opens role dropdown when focused on suggestion -> Arrow keys navigate roles -> Enter selects -> Tab goes to Persist Access toggle -> Space toggles -> Tab reaches SSO pill -> Enter opens SSO panel.

Jess: Great — I'll put that in the component spec.

DesignBot: Automatch suggestion: show top 2 role suggestions based on last used roles for the requesting org and the invitee domain. Confidence score shown as subtle hint. :robot_face:

Tara: Any thoughts on analytics? We should track: role chosen, whether persistent was enabled, SSO pill opened, and whether the audit-jump link was used. That will inform whether the pill is discoverable.

Eli: Also measure keyboard-first flows and usage of the accessibility explainer (the 'i' click).

Jess: Next steps: I'll update the Figma with two variants (compact pill vs inline SSO row) and a short spec for aria labels and keyboard order. Slack review needed by EOD tomorrow. If no major objections, we'll ship as an A/B canary to 10% of orgs.

Sam: Quick checkbox before wrap: aria-labels, focus order doc, analytics events, audit-link format, compact/comfortable setting.

Tara: I'm fine with the plan. +1 to the verb-first copy.

Eli: +1. No blockers from eng side.

Jess: Thanks all — I'll post updated mocks here once they're in Figma. :thumbsup:
